intro: Sizes an oil cooler: heat to reject, stabilised oil temperature and the size needed to hold your target temperature.
flow_hint: Flow sent to the cooler (often 10–25 L/min through the sandwich plate)

r.rating_note: Stabilised temperature compared with the target
r.heat: Heat to reject through the oil
r.eff_note: Share of the temperature difference recovered
r.size_none: Out of reach with this cooler type

warn.impossible: An oil/water cooler cannot go below coolant temperature: aim higher or use an oil/air cooler.
warn.undersized: Cooler too small: increase area, thickness or oil flow, or improve airflow (scoop, ducting).
warn.thermostat: Cooler more than big enough: fit a thermostatic sandwich plate so the oil quickly reaches 90–100 °C.
warn.too_hot: Oil above 130 °C: rapid breakdown and risk to the bearings.
warn.fan: At low speed an oil/air cooler barely cools: fit a fan for stops and queues.
warn.method: Estimate (effectiveness-NTU method): check against the manufacturer's data sheet. Pressure drop not calculated (usually below 0.5 bar).

chart.speed_title: Stabilised oil temperature versus vehicle speed
